definitions.explanation: A mark or impression left by a foot on a surface.
Evidence of someone's passage or activities; figuratively, one's legacy or accomplishments.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}の{上|うえ}に{足跡|あしあと}が{残|のこ}っていた。
examples.english: Footprints were left on the snow.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}の{足跡|あしあと}を{追|お}った。
{彼|かれ}は{歴史|れきし}に{大|おお}きな{足跡|あしあと}を{残|のこ}した。
examples.english: He left a significant mark on history.

notes:
USAGE: {足跡|あしあと} can be literal (physical footprints) or figurative (legacy, traces of activity).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{足跡|あしあと}を{残|のこ}す (to leave footprints; to leave a legacy)
・{足跡|あしあと}を{追|お}う (to follow footprints/trail)
・{足跡|あしあと}を{消|け}す (to erase one's tracks)

ALTERNATE READING: Can also be read as そくせき in more formal or literary contexts, particularly when discussing someone's accomplishments or historical legacy.

RELATED:
・{足取|あしど}り - footsteps, gait; whereabouts
・{痕跡|こんせき} - trace, evidence
